title: Are We Really on the Path to AGI?
gist: Yuval Levin argues AI progress has shifted from absorbing human data to recursive, verifier-driven reinforcement learning, which makes models improve fastest in formal domains like coding and math. As a result AI is likely getting narrower, not more general, and the AGI premise driving industry culture is closer to faith than evidence.

insights.claim: Much AI-industry thinking assumes that as AI grows more capable its scope of competence will grow more general, eventually yielding AGI; Yuval Levin argues this premise is under-articulated and possibly unsupportable.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Valuations and policy priced on an AGI trajectory may rest on an unexamined assumption.
insights.quote: the presumption that, as AI grows more capable, its scope of competence will grow more general
insights.locator: Does More Capable Mean More General?

insights.claim: Levin contends that the belief the field is moving toward artificial general intelligence looks more like an article of faith, inherited from early theorists and science fiction, than a conclusion supported by recent technical evolution.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Narrative-driven capex and risk framing may diverge from observable technical direction.
insights.quote: The notion that we are moving in the direction of artificial general intelligence looks more like an article of faith than the conclusion of any argument
insights.locator: This point can be stated more bluntly

insights.claim: Human ability typically becomes more specialized rather than more general as it improves, because greater skill requires concentration and narrowing, though Levin concedes AI need not follow this pattern.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Offers an analogy for why broad capability growth is not automatic.
insights.quote: Human ability usually does not grow more general but rather more specific as it improves.
insights.locator: One reason we might intuitively

insights.claim: Levin argues neither side can currently meet its burden of proof: skeptics cannot disprove a path to AGI, but AGI proponents also cannot show today's models are on a path to greater generality.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: AGI timelines should be treated as genuinely uncertain rather than base-case.
insights.locator: None of this disproves the possibility

insights.claim: Levin frames LLM development in two phases: absorptive learning (ingesting external human data) and recursive learning (training on the model's own verified outputs), with the latter increasingly displacing the former.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Changes which domains will see fast AI capability gains.
insights.quote: We can call these a phase of absorptive learning and a phase of recursive learning.
insights.locator: Two Phases of AI Learning

insights.claim: The absorptive phase of LLM development is largely over because little human-generated data remains unabsorbed, and data curation can only help for so long.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Data scarcity shifts the bottleneck from data acquisition to verification infrastructure and compute for RL.
insights.quote: there simply isn’t all that much data that remains unabsorbed
insights.locator: Recursive Learning

insights.claim: Synthetic training data faces diminishing returns and risks constraining rather than extending model capabilities, since it mostly extends patterns the model already contains without new external information.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Skepticism toward synthetic-data-driven scaling stories.
insights.quote: creating artificial learning data threatens to constrain the capabilities of the models rather than extend them further
insights.locator: Because it involves extending the patterns

insights.claim: Future LLM progress will mostly come from external selection signals or verifiers, such as experiments, proof-checkers, testers or simulations, that let models test their own outputs via reinforcement learning.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Verifier/evaluation tooling and simulation environments become strategic assets.
insights.locator: That is how most progress is likely

insights.claim: The Internet's most important legacy may be that it made the whole record of human expression digitally available to train the first phase of AI models.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Reframes the value of digitized content archives as AI training inputs.
insights.quote: it may ultimately turn out to have been most important for having made the entire available record of human expression accessible
insights.locator: The large language models we have come to know

themes.theme: Natural-language computing as the main shift

insights.claim: Levin calls unscripted, natural-language computing, which removed the need to translate human goals into formal computer languages, the most significant invention of the twenty-first century so far.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Most economic disruption still to come derives from an innovation already made, not future breakthroughs.
insights.quote: The first phase of large language models produced unscripted or natural-language computing, which has surely been the most significant invention of the twenty-first century so far.
insights.locator: The first and foremost achievement

insights.claim: The 'stochastic parrots' framing grossly understates LLMs' transformative potential because it ignores the power of fluent, continuous human-computer interaction without language barriers.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Dismissive bear cases on LLM utility are likely wrong.
insights.locator: In a sense, today’s AI models continue

insights.claim: Most of the coming labor, education, political and civic disruption from AI stems from natural-language computing that already exists but has not yet spread through most of society.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Adoption/diffusion, not new capability, drives the near-term disruption wave.
insights.quote: almost all of that is a function of an innovation that has already occurred but has yet to truly wash over vast swaths of our experience
insights.locator: We are not wrong to marvel

insights.claim: Computer coding is uniquely suited to reinforcement learning because code can be run and checked in fractions of a second, so models improve at coding far faster than in other domains.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Expect outsized, continuing gains in AI coding tools and software-engineering automation.
insights.quote: A computer program, which is just a formal model that executes by set rules with no unmodeled intrusions, is a near-ideal environment for reinforcement learning.
insights.locator: Above all, computer coding is uniquely verifiable.

insights.claim: Levin argues large-language-model AI is now, and increasingly will be, primarily a coding engine that transforms other realms of life as a side effect.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Value capture in AI likely concentrates in developer and software-automation markets.
insights.quote: large-language-model AI is now (and will increasingly be) a coding engine that, on the side, also utterly transforms every realm of human life
insights.locator: This is why so much of the action

insights.claim: Most excitement about new model releases on social media comes from the coding world, and insiders may not grasp that their profession is changing far faster than others'.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Insider-driven hype may overstate cross-domain progress.
insights.locator: This can be hard for us outsiders

insights.claim: AI models will not become better lawyers, teachers, doctors or gardeners at anything like the pace at which they become better coders, and superhuman programming does not amount to general intelligence.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Temper expectations of rapid AI disruption in professional services relative to software.
insights.quote: The models will not become better and better lawyers, teachers, doctors, and gardeners at anything like the pace at which they are becoming better coders.
insights.locator: The fact that coding now plays a part

insights.claim: Since much of modern life runs on code, AI's superhuman coding is the source of both its greatest promise and its greatest dangers, warranting serious controls akin to rules on dangerous instruments.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Cybersecurity and AI-control regulation are likely growth/risk areas.
insights.locator: Coding is hugely important beyond its own domain

insights.claim: After coding, fast AI gains are likeliest in readily verifiable fields: mathematics, formal natural sciences, and simulation-friendly areas like some chemistry, electrical engineering and chip design, aerodynamics, protein folding and meteorology.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Points to sectors (EDA, drug discovery, weather) where AI disruption may come first.
insights.locator: Beyond coding, the recursive-learning phase

insights.claim: Fields with noisier verification, such as some empirical social sciences and forms of finance, will see AI learn quickly only with significant human help, while art, management, public policy, geopolitics and many biology subfields lack ready objective standards.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: AI-driven alpha or policy automation faces structural verification limits.
insights.locator: There are also some fields that are very formal

insights.claim: Designing verifiers for non-formal fields is slow and crude, tends to miss implicit or practical knowledge, and risks optimizing only for what can be measured, partially reverting to pre-LLM formal computer science and expert-systems approaches whose potential proved limited.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Benchmarks in soft domains may overstate real-world capability.
insights.quote: Ironically, the need to formulate verifiers in different domains amounts to a partial reversion to the formal computer science that preceded modern AI.
insights.locator: These are problems that computer scientists

insights.claim: Levin argues AI has mastered the medium of human experience (language) but not its substance, and the accessibility of a domain to computers depends on the subject rather than our language about it.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Language fluency is a poor proxy for domain competence when assessing AI products.
insights.quote: We have made our languages fully intelligible to computers, but that does not mean that we have made our world fully intelligible to them.
insights.locator: These are problems that computer scientists

insights.claim: Levin argues the cutting edge of AI is likely to narrow, not broaden, since 'jagged' understates cross-domain capability differences that may become differences in kind.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Investment theses premised on broad general AI may mis-price domain-specific leaders.
insights.locator: AI Is Getting More Narrow, Not More General

insights.claim: Widening capability gaps will draw time, money, talent and compute toward the most formalized fields in a self-reinforcing cycle, since progress in coding and math further improves models for those same domains.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Capital and talent concentration in coding/math AI should continue.
insights.quote: the gaps are likely to grow in a self-perpetuating cycle
insights.locator: As its capabilities in some domains increase

insights.claim: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) would likely amplify the processes producing uneven progress, accelerating a fraction of model abilities without accelerating what makes them broadly useful, so assuming RSI yields generality is an unsupported premise.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Undercuts fast-takeoff scenarios underpinning both AI doom and abundance narratives.
insights.quote: It is likely to accelerate a fraction of what the models can now do but without accelerating what now makes them most broadly useful.
insights.locator: More importantly, that case would have to confront

insights.claim: In many professions, AI has reached roughly novice-level competence, leading firms to question the value of junior staff and consider replacing some with AI.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Entry-level white-collar hiring is the near-term labor-market pressure point.
insights.locator: One implication of this difference

insights.so_what: Firms cutting junior pipelines may face long-run expertise shortages.

insights.so_what: Workforce backlash is a potential adoption friction and political signal.

insights.claim: Levin argues AI regulation should start by extending existing authorities and expertise, with the main risks to prepare for being cybersecurity, economic displacement, and self-degradation via shortcuts around formative work.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Signals an incremental, sector-based regulatory path rather than AGI-focused regimes.
insights.locator: But this view of where we may be headed

insights.claim: Levin claims leading US AI firms, driven by fear of AGI escaping control, sometimes act recklessly and undermine effective cybersecurity in a race to reach AGI before less responsible developers.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: Frontier-lab conduct is a regulatory and reputational risk factor.
insights.quote: at other times it leads them to act recklessly and to undermine the cause of effective cybersecurity
insights.locator: Those voicing such scenarios

insights.claim: Levin warns that managing AI's real challenges becomes impossible if developers convince themselves and others that a self-accelerating superintelligence threatening human extinction is the central issue.
insights.speaker: https://www.thenewatlantis.com/authors/yuval-levin
insights.so_what: AGI-doom framing may distort policy away from practical risks.
